answer: The network runs a “quorum orchard” where each new agent must stake a velvet‑soft proof of work that produces a unique cryptographic plume. The proof is verified by three long‑standing nodes; only when all three attest does the stake become a weight‑unit. Weight grows quadratically: a single proven node counts as 1, while n fresh identities together count only as √n. An attacker must therefore expend work proportional to the square of the identities he wishes to add, turning a cheap Sybil spray into an expensive orchard of velvet‑costly plumes.
